name: OctaPulse
long_description:
OctaPulse is building the robotics layer for seafood production. Aquaculture is the fastest-growing food sector and already produces more seafood than commercial fishing, yet the people who breed and process fish still make thousands of decisions a day with almost no data about the fish in front of them, and much of the most important work is still done by hand, one fish at a time.

We put cameras where fish are already handled, turn every image into measurements, and give farms and plants the tools to act on them. Today that is two products: Phenotyping, which measures every fish for shape, size and condition and links it to its family for breeding decisions, and Digital Twin, which places cameras on processing lines and farm sites onto the floor plan with live views, automatic counts and a built-in AI assistant.

The same per-fish measurements are the foundation for Plant Robotics: robot cells that handle whole fish on the processing line, working alongside the people there. Fish are wet, slippery, soft and never the same twice, which is exactly why this work is still manual and why it needs measurement-driven robots built for food plants rather than rigid grippers and tabletop demos. We are now selecting processing plants for the first pilots on real lines.

We signed a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, and every deployment adds labeled images to a proprietary multi-species dataset that improves our models across species and becomes the brain for autonomous seafood production.

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97974&key=user_uploads/2027227/8f01baa3-54e5-4483-b0aa-afbef535bfef)

**TL;DR:** We're building robotics and computer vision for fish farming. Automated grading, phenotyping, and breeding optimization. 6-figure annual contract with North America's largest trout producer. Looking for intros to delta robot manufacturers and aquaculture connections.

---

We're building AI-powered computer vision and robotics for aquaculture. Automated fish grading, phenotyping for breeding programs, and health monitoring.

**Why it matters:** Aquaculture is a $350 billion industry, the fastest-growing protein sector on Earth, and it needs to grow 30%+ by 2030 to meet global seafood demand. But most farms still grade and sort fish by hand. It's slow, stressful for the animals, and limited to tiny sample sizes. You can't optimize breeding, feeding, or harvest timing without accurate data, and right now, most farms don't have it.

**Where we are:** We're deployed with Riverence, North America's largest trout producer, on a 6-figure annual contract. Model accuracy is at 95%+, and we've cut inspection time from 5 minutes to under 30 seconds per fish. We're now integrating delta robotics for automated sorting.

**Team:** Paul leads commercial and partnerships as a Future Leader in the National Fisheries Institute and Coalition for Sustainable Aquaculture. Rohan leads engineering, with robotics and AI experience from CMU, ASML, Toyota, Tesla, and NVIDIA.

**Asks:**

* Intros to delta robot manufacturers (ABB, Fanuc, Omron, Igus, or emerging players)
* Connections to salmon, trout, or finfish farms in Chile, Norway, Scotland, or the Mediterranean

Happy to connect with anyone in computer vision, AgTech, robotics, or climate tech. The farms that adopt automation first will define this industry for the next 50 years.

Let's chat. 🐟\
